title: cairn cleanup clears the finding troubles whose cause is gone
intention: cairn cleanup re-runs the sieve behind each standing finding trouble over the whole repo and clears the troubles whose sieve no longer fires.
why: Measured 2026-11-16: nothing schedules the build inspector's whole-repo sweep, and since 044020db63c0 a one-component run never clears. So inspector-new-finding-history-integrity stood after 74b4209b71ee's dirt was committed (17b738522), until a hand ran the 5m25s sweep and cairn trouble drain. A trouble standing after its cause is gone is a record of truth saying something false (Law 7). cairn cleanup ends every voyage, which is when a fix lands, and its one step was the drain.
traces_to: Law 7: a record of truth stays true; a trouble whose cause is gone must clear. Law 1: the voyage that fixed it should not leave the clear to a hand re-deriving it.
how: inspector.recheck(identities) maps each inspector-new-finding-<sieve> id to its sieve, runs only those sieves over every census component, and sends clear_trouble by exact identity for each sieve with no finding above baseline (the whole-repo reconcile's rule, _standing_finding_ids). --recheck <id>... is its CLI. bin/cmd/cleanup gains a findings step before troubles: it reads cairn trouble live --json and passes the inspector-new-finding-* ids to --recheck, so the drain folds the clears in the same cleanup.

clauses.claim: in a scratch world holding one cleared cause and one standing cause, the recheck clears only the cleared cause's trouble, by its exact identity, and leaves the standing one
the recheck runs only the sieves the troubles name, each over every component
the rule is the whole-repo reconcile's: a sieve firing only at a baselined site clears, and an identity naming no registered sieve is left standing and reported
cairn cleanup hands the recheck every standing inspector-new-finding-* trouble id and only those, before the drain

decisions.text: D1: recheck(identities, root=, baseline_path=) and --recheck in the inspector; returns rechecked, components, cleared, standing, unknown; clears by exact identity via the raiser's clear_trouble.
D2: a red-first proof for clauses 1-3 in a scratch world, scripted census and sieves, recording raiser.
D3: bin/cmd/cleanup gains the findings step before troubles, and its --summarize and --help name it; the bin charter's cleanup entry says two steps.
D4: a red-first proof for clause 4: a scratch copy of bin/cmd/cleanup beside a stub cairn and a stub inspector module.

out: the trouble device's drain and reconcile

measured.saw: inspector-new-finding-history-integrity stood after its cause was committed in 17b738522; it cleared only after a hand ran the whole-repo sweep (5m25s) and cairn trouble drain
measured.how: python3 -m cairn.machines.build_inspector.inspector on the house tree, then cairn trouble live

measured.saw: bin/cmd/cleanup has one step, step troubles "$CAIRN" trouble drain; no ticket or question sets an inspector cadence
measured.how: reading bin/cmd/cleanup; grep of CairnCommons tickets and questions

measured.saw: red on the base: all four teeth red (no recheck in the inspector; cleanup called only the drain)
measured.how: both proofs under bin/cairn test --exec with inspector.py and bin/cmd/cleanup at origin/inspector-reconcile-only-on-sweep

measured.saw: a live recheck of the six standing finding troubles took 33 s in all (component-color 1.6, encapsulation-holds 7.4, diagnostic-mixin 3.0, intention-fidelity 13.9, no-iou-stands 0.1, working-tree-clean 7.0) over 80 components, and every one still stands
